title: TC-EXT-01-U08a is flaky under full-suite concurrency: CaptureServer binds hardcoded TCP port 18181 and its captured headers are read across a thread boundary
registered_by: WF03-ISS-0132-20260807 Step Final (incidental finding during post-rebase verification)
scope: tests/unit/service_task_test.zig — test infrastructure flake, not a production defect.
symptom: `zig build test` intermittently exits 1 with `Build Summary: 81/83 steps succeeded (1 failed); 938/1003 tests passed (64 skipped, 1 failed)`. The failing block is `TC-EXT-01-U08a: executeHttpRequest injects trace, idempotency, and configured headers`, failing at tests/unit/service_task_test.zig:339 on `expectEqualStrings("trace-123", server.first_trace_id[0..server.first_trace_id_len])` — expected `trace-123`, got an empty/short slice, i.e. the CaptureServer thread had not recorded the request headers at the point the assertion ran.
reproduction: Non-deterministic and concurrency-dependent. Observed once in a full `zig build test --summary all` run on branch feature/WF03-ISS-0132-20260807. NOT reproducible in isolation: the compiled binary was run 15 consecutive times directly and passed 15/15; three subsequent full-suite runs on the same branch were clean at 83/83 steps and 939/1003 tests. Six full-suite runs on origin/main (83b88fb) were also clean at 81/81 / 936/1000.
root_cause_analysis: Two independent races, either of which is sufficient. (1) HARDCODED PORT: the test constructs `CaptureServer{ .port = 18181, ... }` and the config's `url_template` hardcodes `http://127.0.0.1:18181/execute`. That port is a shared machine-wide resource. `zig build test` runs many test binaries concurrently, and this repo is routinely checked out twice in parallel workspaces on the same host (see docs note on parallel workspaces / +10 port band), so a bind collision or a connection landing on a foreign listener is possible whenever suite scheduling overlaps. (2) CROSS-THREAD READ WITHOUT SYNCHRONISATION: `server.first_trace_id` / `first_trace_id_len` are written by the CaptureServer's background thread and read by the test thread at line 339. `defer server.join()` runs at scope EXIT — i.e. AFTER all four assertions — so the assertions read fields the server thread may still be writing, with no happens-before edge established between the write and the read. This is a data race by construction; it merely happens to win almost always.
acceptance_criteria: CaptureServer binds an ephemeral port (port 0) and the test reads back the actual bound port to build url_template, rather than hardcoding 18181
The test establishes a happens-before edge before asserting on captured headers (join or an explicit synchronisation primitive) rather than relying on defer-at-scope-exit
The captured-header fields are not read from the test thread while the server thread may still write them
zig build test passes 20 consecutive full-suite runs without this block failing
evidence_file: Observed in run WF03-ISS-0132-20260807 Step Final; failure text captured at tests/unit/service_task_test.zig:339 via std.testing.expectEqualStrings -> error.TestExpectedEqual
notes: Forwarded rather than fixed in WF03-ISS-0132-20260807 per the CLAUDE.md scope boundary: it is an adjacent defect the run noticed, not a blocker of that run's acceptance criteria, and it is unrelated to that run's subject (allocation-failure coverage for parseGraphJson in src/definition/store.zig). That branch changed only src/definition/store.zig, src/definition_store_test_root.zig and build.zig, and does not import or touch tests/unit/service_task_test.zig; adding a build step can perturb suite scheduling and thereby expose this pre-existing race, but is not its cause.
resolution: CaptureServer now binds an ephemeral port (0) instead of hardcoded 18181, reading the actual bound port back via server.socket.address to build url_template dynamically. A std.Io.Event (headers_captured) is set by the server thread immediately after header capture completes and waited on by the test thread before assertions, establishing a happens-before edge that replaces the prior defer-server.join()-at-scope-exit pattern. A second std.Io.Event (listening) similarly gates reading back the bound port. Verified via 5 consecutive isolated runs of zig build test-bpm-src (84/95 pass, 0 fail every run) plus 2 truly-concurrent stress runs reproducing the original full-suite-concurrency scenario -- both clean. Design: src/design/service-task-test-capture-server.md. Test-only change, no production source touched.
